current_evidence: Not verified. The shared WebFetch budget for the session ran out (proxy HTTP 403 'web-fetch budget ... exhausted') before the council's validation-checklist page or PDF could be read; this was not a fault on the council site. Two web searches found no Dudley list newer than the November 2024 checklist.

issues.detail: Grokbot mixed the superseded February 2020 checklist (dmbc-validation-checklist-final-version-feb-2020.pdf) with the November 2024 checklist. Requirements taken from the 2020 document include Contaminated Land, Open space, Planning Statement (change of use and minerals rows), Outline Noise Impact Assessment, Householder Landscaping, and several drawing-standard, CIL and heritage tab items. Their triggers may no longer match the current list.

'Coal Mining / Land Stability Risk Assessment' is listed under Householder, but the trigger Grokbot quotes says householder development is excluded. It is also missing from Full planning and Outline, where it does apply within Development High Risk Areas.
issues.evidence: 'A Coal Mining Risk Assessment will be required with all planning applications for development within these areas (except householder developments).'

issues.detail: 'Planning Statement' is listed under 'Minerals & waste (county)', but the trigger excludes waste management and mineral development. The same row is also placed under 'Change of use - prior approval', although 'change of use applications' in the trigger means major planning applications, not prior approvals. 'Noise Impact Assessment' is placed under Outline only because the text says the assessment 'should outline' noise sources.
issues.evidence: 'All major applications (10 or more dwellings or 1,000 m2 ...) including change of use applications ... except for waste management and mineral development applications'

issues.detail: About 27 requirements are put under 'Full planning' with 'INFERRED: application type not named'. Most of these are triggered by site circumstances rather than application type (for example V29 Arboricultural report where trees are on or next to the site, V18 Ecological survey where protected species may be affected, Heritage Statement for heritage assets and conservation areas, Streetscene where roof heights increase), so they also apply to Householder and Outline. As a result Householder shows only two items, one of them wrong, and Heritage Statement appears only under Listed building consent.
issues.evidence: Heritage trigger: 'required for applications which effect Designated or Non-Designated Heritage Assets including ... proposals in Conservation Areas'

issues.detail: The Flood Risk Assessment trigger runs into the Transport Assessment guidance and stops before the flood-zone conditions. The Design and Access Statement trigger is combined with the elevations requirement and gives no actual DAS trigger. The 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage' row uses text about waste-management facility applications, not refuse storage.
issues.evidence: FRA: 'required for planning applications where the site area is 1 hectare or more in Flood Zone 1 and required for all planning applications Guidance on Transport Assessments...'; Waste: 'All proposals for waste management development (including proposals to expand, upgrade or relocate existing waste facilities)...'

issues.detail: Many triggers are sentence fragments with no threshold or condition: EIA ('require an Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA).'), LVIA ('statements or landscape and visual statements.'), Viability ('to the Viability Assessment also required by this list.'), Planning Obligations ('contribution through a Planning Obligation.'), Block plan ('and Proposed Site Plan (scale 1:500);'), Transport Assessment (thresholds 'set out in appendix B', which was not captured). The Crime prevention, Householder Landscaping and Photographs excerpts mix text from two PDF columns into unreadable text.
issues.evidence: Landscaping (Householder): 'layout and landscape proposals which must changes of use and be fully integrated with proposals for ecological householder enhancement:applications) meeting Within a Conservation Area.'

issues.detail: Grokbot's own extract of V14 'Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) Planning Application - Additional Information Requirements Form and a completed Assumption of Liability Form (Form 1)' (trigger: planning applications that create new retail or residential floorspace) appears only as garbled tab text, not as a requirement row. The Transport Assessment thresholds in Appendix B were not captured. The full set of V-numbered requirements could not be checked against the source in this run.
issues.evidence: tab_items: 'V14 Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) ... Form 1 ... Planning applications ... that create new Retail or Residential floor space.'

issues.detail: Tab items under 'Submission rules' are guidance text and broken URL fragments rather than requirements ('The relevant forms are available at: uestions.pdf', 'And _1_assumption_of_liability.pdf Details of Dudley's CIL charging is available on the Council's website at:', the Historic Environment SPD reference, 'The below checklist should be referred to when submitting a householder application.'). 'Pre-application advice' is advice, not a validation requirement.
issues.evidence: tab_items 'Submission rules' and app_type_rows 'Pre-application advice / engagement details'

issues.detail: Drawing standards are repeated from both the 2020 and 2024 documents (scale lists, 'Scale bars must be provided', location plan scale). One copy is garbled ('Where showor at1:200 least two roads and This is apossible plan...'). 'Cycle parking details' and 'Highways / access details' use the same site-plan fragment ('parking and access arrangements (existing and proposed)'), which is a drawing note rather than a separate requirement.

summary: Grokbot's November 2024 checklist link could not be read or confirmed as current because the session's fetch budget ran out, and searches found nothing newer. Grokbot's extraction mixes in the superseded February 2020 checklist, puts several requirements under application types the source explicitly excludes (Coal Mining under Householder, Planning Statement under minerals/waste), and has many truncated or merged triggers (FRA, DAS, Waste).

withdrawn_issues.detail: The list date is taken from the file name ('nov_2024'), not from the document text. It could not be checked against the document in this run.
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The date basis is indeed the URL. But the date can be checked: the document cover reads "1st November 2024", which matches the recorded 2024-11-01, so the date is correct and only the basis note needs updating.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The workbook stores list dates to the month, so the value is right; only the date-basis label could be better. Not a Grokbot error.
